purpose: Persistent contract workbook health, correctness-risk and calculation-performance evidence.

postAuditAuthorityChange.purpose: Restore the client-approved pre-capacity Transactional DB structure and retain structural-shift expansion in Summit and Excel/VBA.
postAuditAuthorityChange.note: The reserved-capacity prototype is not an authoritative workbook contract.

method.excelTimingScope: Native Excel calculation only; excludes Summit UI, datasource refresh and DevExpress custom-function timing.

unguardedSample.context: INDEX/MATCH against ImportedSchemes without an IFNA guard

macroDisabledRebuildLimitation.reason: Embedded VBA/UDF logic was deliberately not executed during the audit.

findings.title: Summit PMCOST metadata does not match the eight-position compatibility signature
findings.evidence: The workbook has 380 PMCOST calls and passes eight compatibility arguments, but FinalYear is deliberately unused, so seven inputs affect the result. clsPMCost.vb lines 20-27 advertises five value parameters plus two references (seven positions), while lines 85-92 accepts parameters 0 through 7 (eight positions).
findings.implication: DevExpress validation, parsing, or evaluation may diverge from Excel even when current sample values appear to calculate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the eight-position compatibility signature, document that FinalYear is unused, advertise six required value positions plus two required references, and add parity tests before relying on Summit recalculation.

findings.title: Cross-engine UDF parity is not regression-tested
findings.evidence: Development Expenditure contains 380 PMCOST and 380 RESPCOST calls. Summit registers native replacements, but a macro-disabled Excel full rebuild makes seven Check Sheet rows #NAME? while the saved workbook checks are all OK.
findings.implication: Excel/VBA and Summit may produce different values or error behaviour for missing matches, invalid periods, or malformed ranges.
findings.recommendation: Create an automated parity harness comparing the 760 call results and key outputs after Excel/VBA and DevExpress recalculation. Make RESPCOST parameters required if they are unconditionally dereferenced and add explicit error guards.

findings.title: 35,920 formulas depend on worksheet ordering through 3-D references
findings.evidence: Examples include SUM('Component 1:Component 12'!...) and grouped Development/All Schemes blocks.
findings.implication: Moving or inserting a sheet inside or outside a boundary can silently change results without producing a broken reference.
findings.recommendation: Retain these efficient formulas for now, but add an expected sheet-order/block-membership manifest and validate it on open, save, and structural commands.

findings.title: Custom functions perform repeated formula-engine MATCH evaluations
findings.evidence: Both Summit UDF implementations build and evaluate a MATCH expression inside a loop for every call. With 760 workbook calls and up to 40 periods, this can create thousands of nested FormulaEngine evaluations.
findings.implication: This is the most credible Summit-specific calculation hotspot even though native Excel recalculation is already fast.
findings.recommendation: Replace repeated Engine.Evaluate calls with direct range reads and an indexed year-to-rate lookup, preserving Excel MATCH semantics and testing parity.

findings.title: Formula complexity is concentrated and highly repetitive
findings.evidence: There are 6,582 formulas of 500-901 characters, mainly on Development Capital and Development Expenditure. INDEX/MATCH and IF logic dominate the workbook.
findings.implication: Maintenance and structural-change risk are greater than the current timing impact.
findings.recommendation: Refactor only measured hotspots using helper rows/columns or cached match indices. Do not introduce LET/XLOOKUP until the minimum supported Excel version is agreed.

findings.title: Volatile CELL calls are duplicated
findings.evidence: 1,313 CELL occurrences exist: 924 on Hidden - BP Menu Sheet, 388 on Hidden - Sheet Lists, and one on Stress Sensitivity List. The menu formulas call CELL four times per formula to derive a sheet name.
findings.implication: Every recalculation revisits workbook metadata unnecessarily; the current measured impact is modest.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate each CELL result once in a helper cell (or LET only if supported) and reuse it, reducing the menu occurrences by about 75%.

findings.title: Several sheets have inflated used ranges
findings.evidence: 5 Yr Monthly Cashflow uses 337 rows although the last populated row is 102; 5 Yr Quarterly Cashflow uses 262 versus 27. Transactional DB extends to 78 columns while populated content ends at 74.
findings.implication: This can increase rendering, navigation, print, and file-maintenance overhead more than formula calculation time.
findings.recommendation: On a disposable copy, remove only demonstrably obsolete formatting/objects beyond the real model area, then run full Excel/VBA/Summit round-trip tests.

findings.title: One unguarded #N/A remains outside intentional chart suppression
findings.evidence: Of 467 saved formula-error cells, 466 are deliberate NA() chart gaps. Hidden - Tenure Totals Start!B6 is an unguarded INDEX/MATCH #N/A.
findings.implication: The error is currently latent because the saved Check Sheet is OK, but it can leak into future imports or interfaces.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the expected blank-state behaviour and use IFNA/validation if absence from ImportedSchemes is normal.

requiredFutureReview.instruction: Review this evidence and Contract_XLSB_Audit_2026-08-24.md before workbook, calculation engine, Transactional DB, custom-function, structural range, or validation changes.
